::: {.letter-metadata}
**Date:** Feb 1st [1888]  
**From:** Elderfield Otterbourne  
**Manuscript:** MS British Library: Mary Gladstone Papers. Add MSS 46252: 4-5.
:::

My dear [Mrs Drew](people/person_443.qmd)

No book ever was quite equal to the [Conversations with Cousin Rachel](other_books/otherbook_60.qmd), which I believe Masters still publishes. It may here and there seem rather antiquated, but the solid part is of all times. Then there is a little book called [‘Girls’](other_books/otherbook_1049.qmd) - published by Skeffington, and one by Lady Barker, published by Hatchard in connection with [G F S](organizations/other_23.qmd)fr. I cannot recollect its name, but Hatchard’s list gives it.[^1]

As to fiction, girls in their teens seem ready for anything, and the less it is about servants the better they like it - I hardly know what specially to recommend. Esmé Stewart’s [For Half a Crown](other_books/otherbook_1051.qmd)- National Society is a great favourite and [‘A Promise Kept’](other_books/otherbook_1052.qmd) of the same set is very good. The [NS](organizations/other_32.qmd) has published my [‘What to lend - &c’](cmy_books/cmybook_196.qmd)- and you will find a list there

Have you seen the [Mother’s Union Journal](organizations/other_93.qmd)? It is to be quarterly, and costs a penny.[^2] I wish the size could be larger for the money, but it must make its way first. Its first start is very good, I think.

It is to be had of 	[Mr Warren](people/person_2377.qmd) - Printer
High Street
Winchester

Thank you for your kind promise of the address

Yours sincerely
C M Yonge

---

[^1]: Drew had evidently asked for advice books for servant girls. *Conversations with Cousin Rachel* (London: Burns 1844) was an anonymous conduct book by Mary Anne Dyson. *Girls: Their Work and Influence*. Skeffington, 1877 was praised by CMY in *What Books to Lend* (9d.) ‘Practical advice in short compass; excellent for Confirmation gifts.’ The third book was perhaps Amy Susan (Marryat), Lady Baker, *Half-Hours with my Girls, or, ‘Talks about* anything’ (London : Hatchards, 1879).
[^2]: The first issue of the *Mothers' Union Journal* is dated 1888.
